newsitem.title: CHINA: China M2 up 19.1 percent at end-May-newspaper.
newsitem.headline: China M2 up 19.1 percent at end-May-newspaper.

text.p: China's broad M2 money supply was up 19.1 percent year-on-year at the end of May, the Economic Daily said on Friday, quoting figures from the State Statistical Bureau.
China's M1, or currency in circulation plus current business deposits, was up a year-on-year 18.3 percent at the end of May, the newspaper said.
China's M2 was up 20.6 percent at the end of April while M1 at end-April grew by a year-on-year 18.7 percent.
The government has said it expects M2 to grow by 24.5 percent in 1997 and M1 by about 18 percent.
M2 grew by 25.3 percent in 1996 while M1 rose by 18.9 percent, official figures show. M0, or currency in circulation, rose by 11.6 percent last year.
At the end of the first quarter this year, M2 was up 21.1 percent, while M1 was up 18.4 percent and M0 was up 13.6 percent.
